title: Space-time Twin Lab
summary: An interactive special-relativity lab for the twin paradox. Change cruise speed and trip length, then read the worldlines, Lorentz factor, proper time, and reunion age gap together.
technicalDescription: A self-contained HTML, CSS, and JavaScript spacetime diagram models constant-speed flat-spacetime round trips with interactive beta and duration controls, pointer probes, wheel zoom, and linked first-principles calculation walkthroughs.

caseStudy.problem: I want a visual, interactive way to show why a traveler can return younger than an identical twin who stayed on Earth, without burying the geometry in pure algebra.
ownership: Self-contained browser lab with Earth, ship, and light worldlines
Interactive cruise-speed and Earth-frame duration controls
Proper-time readout with Lorentz factor and reunion age gap
Screenshot, GIF, and YouTube media kit for portfolio sync
architecture: Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript served as a same-origin demo under /demos/space-time
Graph hover probes for Earth-frame time and distance
Wheel zoom with reset, plus lesson tabs for calculation walkthrough
decisions: Treat outbound and inbound legs as constant-speed motion with instantaneous turnaround for teaching clarity
Include present-day speed anchors so atmospheric and orbital regimes stay distinct from idealized deep-space cruise
verification: Six live UI screenshots covering default, hover, near-c, longer journey, zoom, and calculation states
Short and detailed YouTube walkthroughs of the running lab
limitations: Teaching model only: no gravity, finite thrust, radiation, energy budget, or biology
At realistic launch and orbital speeds the aging difference is tiny; the twin example uses a high fraction of c for legibility
productionDifferences: A mission design tool would need finite thrust, gravity, and engineering constraints that this lab deliberately excludes
